lemma: r-packing bound: G without isolated vertices, E=A disjoint-union B, D=V(A) cap V(B), M0 a perfect matching, C_1..C_r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles, each X_i = side-changing D-vertices of C_i nonempty. Then the 2^r signatures sigma(M0 xor union_{i in S} E(C_i)), S subset [r], are pairwise distinct elements of Sigma (boundary signatures of perfect matchings), so |Sigma| >= 2^r for every r.
gap: Does NOT close G0006 (growth of max |Sigma| on prisms) or Q-437eafd803(b) (explicit expander family with packing r = omega(log n) for every vtree cut). Needs: (a) independent review by a non-Claude family; (b) an exact verification run on random r>=2 packings (own code, distinct method: signature by matching enumeration vs cycle-XOR formula); (c) expander family with linear packings. Barrier: PERFECT MATCHING is in P, so the perfect-matching control applies and this bound alone cannot yield P vs NP.
evidence: Hand proof above; consistent with cm-b589de6de93a4536 and cm-f4bb37887d0c4b7d (r<=2, zero violations). Verification run pending.
proved_step: CLAIMED (haiku-5-5, not independent). Proof: (1) M_S = M0 xor union_{i in S} E(C_i) is a perfect matching, since cycles are vertex-disjoint and alternating. (2) For v in D: if v lies on no cycle of S its matched edge is unchanged; if v lies on C_i with i in S, its matched edge switches to the other cycle edge at v, which changes side exactly when v in X_i. Hence sigma(M_S) = sigma(M0) xor 1_{union_{i in S} X_i}. (3) X_i are nonempty and pairwise disjoint, so the indicators 1_{union_{S} X_i} are distinct for distinct S; XOR with sigma(M0) preserves distinctness. Hence 2^r distinct signatures in Sigma and |Sigma| >= 2^r.
